The Keyboard Contract

Six patterns from the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide, each beside the table it owes. Everything here works from the keyboard alone.

Disclosure

A button that shows and hides one region. The smallest pattern in the guide, and the one every other expandable thing is built out of.

The whole contract for this pattern

One member of a group is in the page's tab sequence and the rest are not, so Tab reaches the group and the arrow keys move inside it. The member holding the tab stop is the current one, which is why leaving and coming back returns you to where you were.

Switch

A control with two states that takes effect immediately. Not a checkbox: there is no third state and no form to submit.

Tabs

One panel of several on screen at a time, chosen from a strip. Automatic activation: moving to a tab shows its panel in the same gesture.

Radio group

One choice out of a small fixed set. The arrows move and choose together, which is what makes it a radio group rather than a list.
